public_rationale: Microsoft's segment table for the quarter ended December 31, 2024 contains no separate AI segment, supporting the narrow reporting point [e1]. In its January 29, 2025 earnings remarks, Microsoft reported an AI business annual revenue run rate exceeding $13 billion [e2]. Neither disclosure supplies a complete calculation showing which revenue streams enter that figure, so they do not establish whether Microsoft counted anything labelled AI indiscriminately [e1; e2].
limitations: The absence of an AI reporting segment does not establish how the supplemental metric was assembled.
The packet contains no complete inclusion methodology or reconciliation for the AI run rate.
An annual revenue run rate does not establish realized annual revenue or AI profit.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Microsoft's $13bn AI run-rate figure is not a distinct reported segment but a relabelling of anything with AI.

statement.excerpt: There is no "artificial intelligence" part of Microsoft's revenue or earnings. This is literally Microsoft taking anything with "AI" on it and saying "we made money!"

from_speaker: There is no "artificial intelligence" part of Microsoft's revenue or earnings
our_interpretation: The context acknowledges an AI revenue run rate. The fair reading of the first sentence is that AI is not a distinct financial reporting segment, rather than that Microsoft disclosed no AI-related figure.
The second sentence asserts that the run rate is assembled indiscriminately from AI-labelled business. This requires separate evidence about its calculation.
The target is Microsoft's fiscal quarter ended December 31, 2024, identified by the surrounding quarterly figures.
The contract's monetary scope describes the company-reported AI revenue run rate under discussion. Segment financial statements are a different measure and are retained as context.
criteria.support_condition: Financial disclosures show no distinct AI segment, and evidence of the run-rate methodology establishes the asserted indiscriminate aggregation.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Disclosures identify a distinct AI financial reporting segment, or a documented calculation contradicts the asserted indiscriminate aggregation.

evidence.locator: Segment Revenue and Operating Income table and its immediately following explanatory sentence
evidence.explanation: The full table reports Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing; it has no separate AI segment. This establishes the narrow reporting point, but its realized segment figures cannot verify the composition of an annualized AI metric.

Microsoft explicitly disclosed an AI revenue metric alongside its quarterly results. That limits a literal reading of no AI revenue disclosure, but the statement does not show whether the aggregation was indiscriminate.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A methodology and reconciliation for the AI run rate reported with the quarter ended December 31, 2024, identifying included products and revenue streams, inclusion criteria and the annualization method.
